note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: UK: Healey's first Budget DELIVERED Oct 28 — headroom £15B in 2029/30 (vs £23.6B March), OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0% (from 1.6%), 2026 lifted to 1.2%; gilt 10Y -2bp to 5.323%, sterling $1.3298 — the 'boring budget' bond markets wanted (Reuters/XTB). France: Moody's SPARED France (Aa3 affirmed, neg outlook); OAT-Bund ~162bp (Oct 27); revenue-section vote Nov 3; S&P reviews France Nov 27. No US shutdown — CR through Dec 11.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: US Tue beats still underpin the dollar into Thursday's data: durables +1.8%, confidence 91.7 (biggest beat since May 2025), new home sales 676K. US Q3 GDP advance Thu (cons 3.0% SAAR, GDPNow ~3.5-3.6%); EZ/German Q3 GDP Fri; Canada Aug GDP Fri; US jobless claims Thu (198K fcst).
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: AU Q3 CPI hotter than the RBA's path: trimmed +1.0% q/q (Bank forecast 0.8%), Q3 trimmed 3.7% y/y, monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y (vs 4.2% exp) — Nov hike case firms. US Sep PCE Thu (headline +0.5% m/m exp, core +0.3%); EZ flash CPI Fri; German flash CPI Fri; Tokyo CPI Thu evening CT. US CPI 3.7%, import prices +8.1% y/y; BoJ trend index 3.2% y/y in Sep (3-yr high, Reuters Oct 27) cements the Dec BoJ case. BoC MPR: Canada inflation 3.5% by end-2026, 3.1% in 2027, back to 2% only by mid-2028.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: FOMC HELD Oct 28 at 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike) — December hike ~86% (CME post-decision). BoC HIKED Oct 28 to 2.50% (first since July 2023); December further hike ~45%. ECB Thu (hold ~93-97%), BoJ Fri (hold ~98%, Dec hike ~83-88%), RBA Nov 2-3 (hike ~79-85%), BoE Nov 5 (hike ~94%). RBNZ's Oct 28 surprise hold (4-3, 2.75%) delays tightening to Dec 9, not abandons it.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: New CFTC (Oct 20, released Oct 23): euro net short largest since Mar-2020 (contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); hedge funds cut yen shorts, added AUD longs, more bearish CAD (net short largest since early Aug — squeeze fuel into BoC); more bullish GBP. Dollar longs <$40B (down from $44.5B). No crowded-long unwind risk — the pain trade is the euro-short squeeze.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Risk mixed into Super Wednesday: equities steadied Tue (Nasdaq +1.18%, S&P +0.60%; KOSPI +6%+ in Asia on SK Hynix) but the Gulf bid is back — Houthis claim a missile hit on Saudi's biggest refinery (550k bpd, unconfirmed by Saudi); WSJ via TradingView: US told Gulf nations to be ready for a fresh Iran campaign after the midterms. Shekel -1% to 3.084 as the Israel count (~42%) confirmed a deadlock (Netanyahu bloc 57, opposition 47, Arab 16; official results Nov 4). Dollar at a two-week high (102.40) — the haven bid is in the dollar this time, not just the yen.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Brent $115.36 (+1.3%) / WTI $101.12 (+1.22%) in Asia (Reuters 0140 GMT Oct 28) — rebound after Tuesday's ~$2 drop, on the unconfirmed Saudi refinery claim; spread ~$14.24. API crude drew -2.031M bbls (vs +0.5M exp); EIA due 9:30am CT. Net importers (EUR/JPY) still pay the tax; exporters (AUD/CAD) get the tailwind.
tot.title: Terms of trade
